filters.notes: resolved via gender dict at runtime

join_order.notes: Use _idx/movie_companies__company_id__{offsets,rowids}.bin; collect candidate movie_ids into mv_set (hash_set) plus cn_ids small bitset/array. Expected candidate movies ~ a few thousand.
For each mv: lo=off[mv], hi=off[mv+1]; require any keyword_id in k_ids (small set: hash_set or sorted linear). Retain mv that pass; semi-join.
For each mv: scan range; require info_type_id==it1_id AND info IN ('Horror','Thriller') (memcmp on off/dat). Captured rows feed MIN(mi.info) and define surviving mv_set for next steps.
For each surviving mv: scan range; require info_type_id==it2_id. Capture mi_idx.info for MIN(mi_idx.info).
For each mv: scan range; require ci.note IN 5 writer literals (varlen compare via off/dat); fetch person_id.
Lookup name.gender[pid]==m_code; if pass, fetch name via name.{off,dat}; feed MIN(n.name).
Once mv qualifies (at least one ci+name passes), fetch t.title[mv-1] for MIN(t.title). t.id is identity, so movie_id maps directly.

data_structures.m_code: int8 scalar from gender dict resolve
data_structures.mv_set_candidates: flat_hash_set<int32> (or sorted vector) sized to a few thousand initial
data_structures.aggregation: scalar MIN registers: 4x (varlen current best + length); use lexicographic memcmp; thread-local then merged

parallelism.notes: cn_ids is tiny (~10); parallelism is more useful inside: after gathering candidate movie_ids, distribute mv_set across threads via morsel_driven loop. Each thread maintains local MIN registers; final reduction across threads. Avoid parallel scan of giant cast_info because we drive by mv ranges (index_nested_loop), naturally bounded.

indexes.purpose: drive from cn_ids to candidate movie_ids
range scan mk rows per mv for keyword_id semi-check
range scan mi rows per mv for info_type+info filter
range scan mi_idx rows per mv for info_type filter
range scan ci rows per mv for note+person_id
